business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electronic Catalog Retail of Industrial Maintenance Hardware

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state company law variations)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (French Napoleonic commercial codes with Germanic statutory overlay; EU law primacy)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–China Comprehensive Tax Treaty (signed 1994, in force 1996, as modified by the BEPS Multilateral Instrument)
Luxembourg–Hong Kong Tax Treaty (signed 2007, in force 2010)
Luxembourg–United States Tax Treaty (signed 1996, as amended by the 2009 Protocol)
EU–China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (signed 30 December 2020, ratification pending)
Benelux Economic Union (Treaty of The Hague, revised 2008)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended by the Laws of 13 February 2018 and 25 March 2020 (transposing EU Directives 2015/849, 2018/843 and 2018/1673); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), implemented by Grand-Ducal Regulation of 28 January 2019; Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended by the Law of 12 July 2013 (governing the SCSp); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Commercial and Companies Register (RCS); EU Council Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 and UN consolidated sanctions lists; CSSF Regulation 12-02, as amended.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (public access suspended after ECJ joined cases C-37/20 and C-601/20 of 22 November 2022; access for CSSF, FIU, tax authorities, bailiffs, and regulated financial institutions remains; a restricted 'legitimate interest' access route for journalists and civil society persists)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / excerpt from the foreign company register of the corporate general partner (if the GP is a non-Luxembourg entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the general partner's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Luxembourg is a Contracting Party to the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the power of attorney granted to the Luxembourg incorporator, notary or legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the principal's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, followed by certified translation into French, German or English

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport (or national identity card) of each intended UBO, general partner and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or notary public in the country of issuance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or certified copy by a Luxembourg notary if the original is presented in person

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, issued within the last 3 months) of each UBO and signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public utility company or regulated credit institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization if the issuing state is not a Hague Convention member; otherwise notarized copy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming the origin of funds and absence of adverse AML findings (required where initial contributions are wired before registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Regulated credit institution in the principal's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank-stamped original accepted by Luxembourg notaries; additional Luxembourg notarial certification may be required by the receiving bank

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax residence certificate of the corporate general partner (substance and treaty documentation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent tax authority of the general partner's country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all general partners, limited partners, UBOs and authorized signatories against: (i) UN Security Council consolidated lists; (ii) EU Council restrictive measures (Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 and autonomous listings); (iii) Luxembourg RBE disqualification flags and CSSF sanction notices; (iv) OFAC SDN list for USD-denominated SWIFT wires; (v) PEP status as defined in Article 2(1)(13) of the AML/CFT Law, including family members and close associates, with Enhanced Due Diligence and source-of-wealth/source-of-funds verification required for non-EEA PEPs; and (vi) adverse media review on recognized commercial screening databases. The SCSp is classified Low_Risk_Standard for ISIC 4791 B2B MRO e-commerce, but the statutory CDD and transaction-monitoring obligations under the 2004 Law apply irrespective of the risk tier.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – eRegistre / RCS online portal (www.lbr.lu); electronic filing of incorporation instruments is available under the Law of 4 November 2020 on digital incorporation and filing.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name of an SCSp must be preceded or followed by the token 'SCSp' or the unabbreviated phrase 'Société en Commandite Spéciale'. Names may be expressed in French, German, Luxembourgish, English or any Latin-script language; non-Latin names must be transliterated into Latin characters in the deed. The name must contain at least one distinctive alphabetic element versus all names already recorded in the RCS, must not be misleading as to the form, activity or nationality of the entity, and must not contravene public order or good morals.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank (requires prior CSSF or ECB authorization)
Assurance / Insurance / Réassurance (requires Commissariat aux Assurances authorization)
Fonds / Fund / OPC / SICAV (implies regulated collective investment scheme; requires CSSF registration or AIFM licensing)
Luxembourg / État / Grand-Duché / Commune / Chambre de Commerce (implies official state or municipal connection; requires ministerial approval)
Holding / Fiduciaire / Audit / Avocat (implies regulated professional activity without the corresponding license)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Luxembourg does not operate a statutory name-reservation system; name clearance is obtained at the moment the RCS registers the incorporation deed. If the RCS registrar refuses registration on grounds of name conflict or misleading character, the incorporator or notary may: (1) request a written statement of reasons within 8 days of the refusal; (2) amend and re-file the deed with a corrected name without additional notarial fees if the initial notarial engagement so provides; and (3) appeal a definitive refusal by petition to the First Chamber of the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within 15 days of notification, heard in summary proceedings. A favorable judgment is transmitted to the registry as an enforceable order. De facto priority over later identical name filings accrues from the date and time of the first valid RCS receipt.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted with conditions. The SCSp must maintain a registered office in Luxembourg capable of receiving official notifications and judicial service. A virtual or domiciliation office is acceptable only when operated by (i) a Luxembourg law firm, (ii) a chartered accountant (expert-comptable), or (iii) a commercial domiciliation company approved by the Ministry of Justice under the Law of 31 May 1999 regulating the domiciliation profession. For an ISIC 4791 B2B MRO catalog e-commerce business, a domiciliation address with mail-forwarding and administrative support is commercially standard and does not impair the SCSp's legal existence. However, to preserve EU tax treaty access and avoid characterization as a letterbox entity, the SCSp should maintain at least an invoicing function, a local decision-making contact, and accounting records held in Luxembourg; a purely passive virtual mailbox without any administrative mandate is insufficient for substantive residency claims.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate, estimated at 20–30% within the first 24 months of operation. The RBE registrar, CSSF-licensed banks and payment processors conduct documentary oversight; the Luxembourg direct tax administration performs occasional unannounced substance visits in e-commerce structures, and the VAT authorities may carry out premises inspections where intra-EU distance-selling thresholds are exceeded. The Low_Risk_Standard AML tier reduces the probability of inspection, but the risk rises if the entity registers for VAT in multiple EU Member States or trades MRO parts with dual-use characteristics.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory LBR fee schedule (EUR 20–75 depending on annex pages; mid-range estimate converted at EUR/USD 1.08)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a non-regulated SCSp without real-estate contribution: EUR 1,100–1,400 all-inclusive of statutory disbursements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO initial declaration to the RBE (filed by the notary upon incorporation)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed domiciliation agent or law firm in Luxembourg City
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market tariff for low-risk trading entities: EUR 1,500–2,400 per year, including mail handling and regulatory notification forwarding

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague apostille, notarization, and certified translation of foreign corporate documents and identity/address bundles
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authorities in countries of origin and sworn translators
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Average mixed tariff: EUR 15–45 per apostille, EUR 30–80 per notarial certification, EUR 20–60 per translated page; estimated 8–10 documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a custom SCSp partnership agreement with multiple limited partner classes: EUR 1,900–2,600

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 944-1 to 944-32 (SCSp regime introduced by Law of 23 July 2016); supplemented by Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of Articles of Association (Acte de constitution - Statuts) together with RCS Form A registration application
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital and no escrow account requirement under the SCSp regime (Article 944-2 of the 1915 Law); partners freely fix their contributions, payable in cash or in kind.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Approved unanimously by the general partner and the partners of the SCSp: (1) the final Articles of Association, initialed for identification, are approved and shall be signed before a Luxembourg notary; (2) the registered office is established at [registered address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; (3) the general partner's subscription of its interest is ratified, no minimum paid-in capital being legally applicable; (4) [Name] is appointed Gérant, with full management power over the B2B MRO catalogue platform within the corporate object (ISIC 4791); (5) authorization is granted to execute all RCS, RESA, RBE and tax formalities and to appoint the professional advisers and accountants.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial execution of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All general and limited partners must appear before a Luxembourg notary to sign the Articles of Association. The notary verifies legal capacity, the corporate object covering ISIC 4791 e-commerce, and any powers of attorney. For corporate partners, a certificate of legal existence is required. The notary files the deed for subsequent RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Final draft Articles of Association with SCSp clauses
Valid passports or ID cards of all partners
KYC documents and source-of-funds statements
Certificate of legal existence for corporate partners (extrait du registre)
Power of attorney if any partner acts by proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Queries by the notary are cured by drafting a private addendum or rectification deed; the formal signing session is rescheduled within 24 hours; any detected legal incapacity requires replacement of the partner before re-execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription of partnership interests and payment of contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Paying bank in Luxembourg or notary's escrow account (no state-administered escrow)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Partners transfer their agreed contributions, typically via SWIFT, to the SCSp's designated Luxembourg bank account or to the escrow account held by the notary. No minimum capital is checked. The notary or the Gérant records the equity subscription schedule and confirms payment through a banker's attestation.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening confirmation or attestation de blocage
Equity subscription schedule signed by the general partner
Proof of SWIFT transfer or valuation report for in-kind contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If contribution is pending, the notary inserts a suspensive condition in the deed; funds are re-routed through the SWIFT network and the banker's attestation is reissued within one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing and registration with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of notarial signature, file via the LBR online portal the notarised Articles of Association together with RCS Form A. The electronic filing fee is paid online. The registrar verifies the legal form and corporate object and issues the registration certificate (extrait) with the RCS registration number.
required_dossiers: Notarised Articles of Association (acte de constitution)
RCS Form A duly completed
Proof of online fee payment
Extract of the criminal record of the Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: RCS queries are cured by filing a signed explanatory note or a notarial addendum; the notary coordinates a corrected submission; resubmission is completed within five working days without loss of priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal publication in the RESA official gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — RESA (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary transmits the formation deed and RCS registration confirmation for electronic publication in RESA. Publication in the official gazette creates the legal effects of the registration against third parties. The registry issues a proof of publication extract.
required_dossiers: Notarised Articles of Association
RCS registration certificate (extrait)
Publication request form transmitted by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Refusal of publication due to formal defects is cured by the notary correcting the deed and resubmitting a rectified act; legal effectiveness is postponed until the new publication is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) and Administration des contributions directes (ACD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the initial VAT registration form through Guichet.lu or the AED form 010. Because the SCSp is tax-transparent, the partners' tax statuses govern direct taxation, while the partnership itself normally obtains a Luxembourg VAT number and EORI number if goods are imported. The ACD issues the national taxpayer reference.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Notarised Articles of Association
Identification of all partners and their residence certificates
EORI application if importing MRO goods
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the file is rejected for missing partner details, submit a supplement within five working days; a provisional VAT number may be issued pending verification and late penalties are waived on voluntary correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) declaration to the RBE
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) — Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCS registration, file the beneficial ownership declaration identifying any individual exercising ownership or control of more than 25% of the partnership, including the general partner. The declaration is filed online through lbr.lu and the filing confirmation is kept.
required_dossiers: RBE electronic declaration form
Copy of identification documents of each UBO
Updated ownership structure chart
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of a registry query, submit a corrected RBE declaration promptly; voluntary rectification within the legal deadline removes risk of administrative fines and preserves access to financing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy — Industry and Commerce Division (Ministère de l'Économie, Direction de l'industrie)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — electronic catalogue retail of industrial MRO hardware is a non-regulated service activity requiring only the RCS registration; no industrial operating licence, manufacturing authorisation or commercial permit is required under Luxembourg law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement — Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the pure e-commerce platform has no industrial installation requiring a full EIA report or EIA registration; if the SCSp operates a physical warehouse, only communal building permits and packaging-waste registration apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No applicable industrial discharge thresholds for the online platform; for any operated warehouse: zero industrial wastewater discharge, VOC emissions below 2 kg/day under the EU Solvent Emissions Directive regime, and packaging waste management in accordance with the Luxembourg Code de l'environnement (waste codes 15 01 01 and 15 01 02).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Communal fire safety inspection of the head office and any warehouse, supported by an OAI technical control attestation for the building; occupational workplace clearance issued by the ITM (Inspection du Travail et des Mines) covering e-commerce staff and logistics areas, including first-aid and electrical installation checks.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct taxes and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; official e-government portal: myguichet.lu; direct tax portal: impotsdirects.public.lu; VAT portal: enregistrement.public.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg SCSp carrying on taxable economic activity: (1) obtain RCS matricule registration through the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés / myguichet.lu if the SCSp has Luxembourg establishment, activity, or certain transactions requiring registration; (2) apply to the AEDT for VAT identification via myguichet.lu using the VAT registration application, submitting the RCS extract, partnership agreement, proof of registered office or non-resident address, manager/partner identity documents, and estimated turnover; (3) AEDT issues a Luxembourg VAT identification number in the format LU + 8 digits; (4) a non-established taxable person must, where required, appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative before registration; (5) use the assigned number for periodic VAT returns, recapitulative statements, and Intrastat declarations where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: the SCSp is fiscally transparent for Luxembourg direct taxes (corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax); partners are taxed directly on their profit shares. For VAT, the SCSp is a separate taxable person to the extent it makes taxable supplies in its own name; if economically inactive, no VAT registration is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not have a US-style check-the-box regime. The SCSp's transparency is the statutory default. Under Article 175 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law, a qualifying commercial partnership carrying on a commercial activity whose partners are all taxable corporate entities may opt to be treated as a fully taxable entity, subject to AEDT approval and ongoing compliance; the election does not alter VAT treatment. Hybrid mismatch rules are applied to prevent non-taxation where Luxembourg classification differs from foreign classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Luxembourg Value Added Tax (TVA) under the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979, as amended, implementing Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general turnover threshold for taxable persons established in Luxembourg; any taxable economic activity requires VAT registration. A simplified small-enterprise franchise exemption applies to locally established taxable persons whose annual taxable turnover does not exceed EUR 30,000, subject to compliance conditions; for intra-Community distance sales by non-established e-commerce suppliers, the EU EUR 10,000 annual Union distance-selling tolerance applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: As of 2025, Luxembourg does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or invoice-by-invoice API approval regime. B2G e-invoicing is mandatory through the PEPPOL network. From 1 January 2026, domestic B2B e-invoicing will be mandatory for taxpayers established in Luxembourg; invoices must be exchanged in a PEPPOL-compliant structured electronic format and transmitted through the Luxembourg national e-invoicing platform. No pre-clearance or tax-stamping requirement exists, but exchange data must be retained for VAT audit and recapitulative reporting.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of industrial MRO goods by a Luxembourg SCSp is eligible for Luxembourg 0% VAT only if the goods are physically dispatched or transported outside the European Union by the supplier or for the supplier's account, and the supplier holds conclusive evidence that the goods left the EU no later than 90 days after supply. The customer must be a non-EU purchaser for direct export, or an EU taxable person acting in good faith where an exempt intra-Community dispatch is validly established. The supply must be supported by an accepted customs export declaration and transport proof. Supplies of digital catalog services or services unrelated to the exported goods remain taxable at the applicable Luxembourg rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Proof of Physical Export (CMR/Air Waybill/FIATA or carrier statement)
Non-EU Customer Purchase Order or Supply Contract
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT has broad audit powers to cross-check export declarations, transport documents, bank settlement, and VAT returns with customs data. Where zero-rating cannot be substantiated, the AEDT reassesses output VAT at 17% plus default interest (currently 0.6% per month) and applies administrative fines of up to 10% of the tax for good-faith errors. Fraudulent export claims, forged documents, or circular transactions trigger higher penalties, criminal fines, imprisonment, a clawback period extended to ten years, and joint liability of directors, tax representatives, and service providers; in ordinary cases the clawback period is five years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting within the Eurosystem framework and the European Central Bank (ECB); external financial conduct and AML supervision is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). There is no standalone foreign exchange administration in Luxembourg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current and capital account convertibility is guaranteed under EU Treaty provisions on free movement of capital and payments and the euro monetary regime. Luxembourg maintains zero exchange controls; no repatriation, approval, or licensing hurdles exist for dividend, interest, fee, or profit remittances from an SCSp. Remittances are subject only to standard AML/KYC screening and, where applicable, EU sanctions and tax formality obligations (e.g., withholding tax certification, beneficial ownership documentation).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender requirements, no compulsory conversion ratios, and no repatriation timelines. Euro-denominated and foreign-currency export receipts may be retained freely, held in correspondent accounts, or converted at market rates through any licensed EU payment institution or commercial bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (multi-currency EUR/USD/CHF) and segregated Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account with SWIFT corporate access; Capital Escrow Account for partnership commitments
Corporate Operational Account and special-purpose escrow account for SCSp capital subscriptions

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Kredietbank S.A. Luxembourgeoise (KBL) / Quintet Private Bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Private banking service for SCSp treasury; multi-currency standby facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High, but subject to strict legal boundaries. Luxembourg-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) under the CSSF regime may provide multi-currency corporate e-wallets, but they are not licensed to grant credit and often cannot offer full commercial letters of credit or trade instruments. Offshore digital EMIs without a Luxembourg or EU passport are generally not viable for an SCSp due to EBA regulatory expectations, local substance requirements, and bank-correspondent due diligence; unlicensed foreign EMIs must be avoided for treasury liquidity. A CSSF-authorised EMI or an EU-pasporting EMI can serve payment-rail purposes for MRO catalogue collections and disbursements, but the primary operating account must remain at a fully supervised credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law does not impose a fixed statutory requirement for all directors to appear physically before the bank, and remote video-KYC is accepted by most major Luxembourg credit institutions. However, in practice CSSF circular KYC/AML expectations and bank internal policies generally require at least one senior manager or authorised representative with apparent authority for the SCSp to attend an initial physical or secure video meeting. For SCSp structures, banks will also require the general partner (or its legal representative) to provide identification, proof of authority, and corporate documentation. Fully remote opening through online portals is possible only where the bank offers a streamlined digital onboarding for EU-regulated structures and the SCSp has no adverse risk flags; otherwise a physical or notarised signature is mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership chain of the SCSp, especially nominal non-resident limited partners and silent participation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide an annotated organisational chart from ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) to each limited partner; notarised partnership agreement with economic substance statements; audited NAV reports; regulatory filings demonstrating tax transparency; CSSF-compliant UBO declaration; bankers' references for all material partners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industrial MRO catalog e-commerce transactions lacking physical supply-chain visibility
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply contracts, vendor invoices, warehouse logistics evidence (customs declarations, bills of lading, delivery receipts), quality control inspection reports, insurance certificates for goods, and historical trading records proving genuine commercial activity in industrial maintenance hardware.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of third-party payment aggregators and credit card settlement for cross-border B2B sales
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant acquiring agreements, settlement statements from licensed PSPs, chargeback history, PCI-DSS attestation, reconciliation ledger, and evidence that card settlement rails are used only for permissible low-risk electronic retail transactions, with predominant B2B settlement via SWIFT or commercial LC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity inbound capital subscriptions and rapid outbound trade disbursements resembling pass-through laundering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital call notices, subscription agreement, disbursement schedule matched to purchase orders, no-commingling ledger, bank-level liquidity report, board-approved treasury policy, and sworn statement on source of funds for each limited partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-jurisdiction nexus where the SCSp is managed by a non-Luxembourg entity or where limited partners are in high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Central administration and registered office certificates, substance documentation (minutes, premises lease, payroll), tax residence certificate of the general partner, country-specific risk mitigation, enhanced due diligence files, and independent legal opinion that the SCSp is not used to circumvent sanctions or tax laws.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions to the SCSp must be initiated via SWIFT MT103 from the limited partner's bank, with precise value-dating instructions to the Luxembourg counterparty bank (LUX IBAN), and must reference the partnership's capital call notice and the purpose code 'IFZ' or 'General capital contribution to a partnership' in EU statistical terms. Contributions received from non-EU jurisdictions are cleared through the correspondent banking network (e.g., CHIPS, Fedwire) and credited in EUR after any necessary TARGET2 settlement. For funds above €10,000 or from non-EEA parties, banks require a copy of the capital call, identification of the remitter and ultimate originator, and confirmation that the contribution is recorded as paid-in capital in the SCSp ledger. No exchange control permission is required; however, TARGET2/SWIFT message and sanctions screening must clear. SEPA CT (SEPA Credit Transfer) may be used for EUR injections from EEA bank accounts; wire transfer must include legal entity identifier (LEI) or SWIFT BIC of the partnership to avoid blocked credits.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Payments to suppliers for industrial MRO procurements are executed by SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) with accompanying commercial documentation (invoice, packing list, contract) available to the remitting bank. Larger contract values and open-account terms may also use documentary letters of credit (Commercial LC, UCP 600) issued by Luxembourg banks, with export/import settlements routed through TARGET2 or major clearing systems. For intra-EU trade, SEPA Direct Debit or SEPA CT is permissible; for non-EU suppliers, the standard rail is an MT103 with appropriate payment purpose code (e.g., 109 for supplies/goods) and a smooth S.W.I.F.T network. Outbound disbursements from the Capital Escrow Account require matching to treasury policies, and over a threshold (typically €50,000 cumulative per day) the bank may request the underlying purchase order and proof of trade to maintain low-risk AML standing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EU-market standard FX Forward contracts with maturity up to 12 months, executed under ISDA/CSSF-compliant master agreements with Luxembourg or OECD counterparty banks
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for certain excluded currencies where delivery is unavailable; subject to institutional counterparty eligibility and not prohibited by BCL/ECB regulations
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF) for long-term liquidity hedging of multi-currency MRO collections
FX spot transactions through authorised credit institutions; no mandatory interbank central clearing for micro/mid-sized treasuries
Option-based EUR/USD collars (purchased options) permitted for hedging known procurement exposures, provided no speculative leverage is introduced into the SCSp treasury

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RBE confirmation of ultimate beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the anniversary of the latest UBO declaration; every calendar year; amended declaration within one month after any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted confirmation exposes the general partner and relevant officers to criminal fines ranging from EUR 125 to EUR 250,000; a court may impose coercive penalties and order corrective filing; persistent default following formal notice may result in strike-off of the RCS registration.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at SCSp entity level (tax transparent). For a fully taxable Luxembourg S.A./S.à r.l., the CIT headline rate is 17% plus 7% solidarity surcharge, giving 18.19%; adding Luxembourg City municipal business tax yields a combined top effective rate of approximately 24.94%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is exempt from entity-level CIT, municipal business tax and net wealth tax. Profits are allocated to partners and taxed in their hands. Eligible corporate partners may access the Luxembourg participation exemption and the IP box regime (80% deduction of qualifying IP income), producing a materially lower effective tax burden for qualifying B2B MRO e-commerce activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Luxembourg partnership income-allocation return (transparent SCSp statement) filed via the Administration des Contributions Directes 'MyTax' secure e-filing portal, available through guichet.lu. Form 540 is used only for fully taxable capital companies, not for the SCSp itself.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; partners settle their tax liabilities through quarterly instalments based on assessed allocable income.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the return and allocation schedule must be filed no later than 31 December of the following year. Non-calendar fiscal years follow the adopted accounting period and Luxembourg tax assessment practice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp name, RCS registration number, Luxembourg tax number, legal form SCSp, registered office, and NACE code 47.91 / ISIC 4791 for electronic retail of industrial MRO hardware.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the Luxembourg authorised representative or tax agent details; confirm a valid Luxembourg registered address and resident general partner for filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year opening and closing dates, number of months, and accounting currency in EUR.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the SCSp fiscal year consistently; non-resident partners must report the same period and convert foreign currencies at the applicable ECB or official exchange rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net book profit/loss before tax, including B2B MRO catalogue sales, cost of goods sold, warehousing, freight, payment processor fees and overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude Luxembourg VAT where chargeable; describe the MRO supply chain and state whether cross-border sales are subject to OSS or reverse-charge treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Each partner's name, country of residence, tax identification number, profit share percentage and allocated taxable income or loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach tax residence certificates (TRC / Form 22) for all non-resident partners claiming treaty benefits; the SCSp does not withhold WHT on profit allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Values of all controlled transactions with affiliated suppliers, service providers, logistics platforms and group financing entities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the OECD transfer-pricing method selected (typically TNMM for B2B catalogue distribution); attach Local File and Master File if thresholds are exceeded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income, foreign permanent establishments and foreign withholding taxes subject to DTA credit or exemption.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File Form 22 and supporting tax vouchers if foreign tax credits are claimed; ensure treaty relief is claimed in the partner's home jurisdiction, not at the SCSp level.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incomplete filing exposes the SCSp to ex-officio assessment and a 10% late-filing surcharge (minimum EUR 50), plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.6% on unpaid taxes. Wilful concealment may trigger criminal tax fraud proceedings with fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to five years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on SCSp profit distributions because the SCSp is tax transparent and its allocations are partnership profit distributions, not dividends. The standard Luxembourg dividend WHT is 15% for capital companies, reducible to 0% or 5% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive and DTA relief where substance and holding-period requirements are satisfied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No WHT is withheld on SCSp distributions. If a Luxembourg subsidiary pays dividends through the structure, the beneficial owner must submit a Form 22 tax residence certificate, a beneficial-ownership declaration, and the applicable Form 21/withholding-exemption claim to the paying agent before distribution. Excess WHT may be reclaimed by filing a refund claim with the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration, generally before 31 December of the year following the income year.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Outbound royalties: 0% statutory withholding tax in Luxembourg; no treaty withholding tax is generally imposed. Outbound interest: 0% statutory withholding tax, with limited exceptions for certain bonds and variable-yield revenue instruments at 15%; treaty rates on interest are generally 0% or reduced under Luxembourg's DTA network.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000 group consolidated turnover for the Master File; EUR 1,000,000 aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions for the Local File; Country-by-Country reporting is mandatory at EUR 750,000,000 group turnover. These threshold references align with Luxembourg's application of Article 56bis LIR and OECD TP Guidelines.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not enact separate Economic Substance Regulations of the offshore type. However, the doctrine of abuse of law, BEPS minimum standards and EU ATAD GAAR require an SCSp to show genuine business activity, local management decision-making, premises, and a commercial rationale. An SCSp engaged in MRO e-commerce must have real substance; otherwise the tax administration may disregard the entity and reattribute its profits to the place of effective management or to the beneficial owners.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a false or incomplete Luxembourg partnership allocation return, deliberately omitting B2B MRO sales, manufacturing fake cost entries, or maintaining undisclosed foreign payment accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to five years; civil reassessment on presumed income; 10% late-filing surcharge; monthly late-payment interest at 0.6%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers, authorized signatories and tax representatives who sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for evaded tax. Courts may impose travel bans, asset freezing, and extradition under EU and mutual legal assistance instruments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Luxembourg SCSp with no office, no employees, no independent bank account and no local decision-making solely to obtain Luxembourg treaty benefits on industrial MRO e-commerce income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the SCSp for tax purposes, reallocation of income to the jurisdiction of effective management, denial of DTA benefits, additional tax assessments, and application of abuse-of-law penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners may become personally liable for restored tax and penalties when partnership assets have been stripped or transferred; criminal liability for fraud may include imprisonment and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare required Master File / Local File, pricing MRO resales below arm's length, routing excessive management or IT fees to foreign affiliates, or failing to document selection of the TNMM/CUP method.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upward adjustment of taxable income, denial of deductions, penalties up to 10% of the tax deficit (up to 50% for gross negligence and 100% for wilful deceit), and monthly interest of 0.6%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve materially false TP documentation are jointly liable for additional corporate and municipal tax; serious cases attract criminal fines, imprisonment, and piercing of the SCSp veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register the ultimate beneficial owner of the SCSp in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners, submitting stale or false RBE data, or failing to conduct CDD on non-resident partners involved in the B2B MRO trading platform.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 1,250,000 or 10% of annual turnover under Luxembourg AML law; public publication of non-compliance; criminal imprisonment up to five years for money-laundering offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Natural persons responsible for AML compliance are personally liable; corporate-veil defenses are unavailable in criminal proceedings; foreign authorities may issue travel bans and extradition requests through mutual legal assistance.
